column1: # Diet dishes (diet-dishes/2): preparations and dishes that hold what a severe restriction restricts by their definition, derived rather than added by example (staging checkpoint 6, R5: "six toasts", "narrow wafers", "half a pint of Madeira sauce", "caper sauce" and "vinaigrette" were shown to the types they hold).

# dish: the name as read, lower case, singular. names: other names and spellings, joined by |. made of: what the definition makes it of, joined by |: a word the restriction patterns read (wheat flour, butter, egg yolk, vinegar) or another dish of this file, whose contents it takes (Madeira sauce is demi-glace and Madeira; demi-glace is espagnole; espagnole is a brown roux of butter and wheat flour). DietDishes resolves every dish to the words it holds; a restriction type whose pattern reads one of them holds the dish's patterns (DefaultRestrictionCriteria.CompositeCompanions), like a composite of label-terms.tsv.

# Sources, all in the public domain: ESCOFFIER = A. Escoffier, A Guide to Modern Cookery (1907, the English edition of Le Guide Culinaire, 1903), the chapter on sauces: the leading sauces (espagnole, velouté, béchamel, tomato) and the small sauces made from them. A dish may be made of a composite of label-terms.tsv (roux, espagnole, veloute, bechamel sauce, supreme sauce, sponge cake, ladyfinger, custard), whose contents it takes. FARMER = Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896): sauces, batters, pastry, toast, fritters. BEETON = Isabella Beeton, The Book of Household Management (1861): melted butter, caper sauce, forcemeat. WEBSTER = Webster's Revised Unabridged Dictionary (1913): the definition of the word. 21CFR = Title 21, Code of Federal Regulations (166.110 margarine: edible fat or oil with water, milk or milk products). LABEL = the ingredient statement of the leading brand, as USDA FoodData Central's branded file publishes it. ARTUSI = Pellegrino Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891).
